items.scene: We can see shapes in people, animals, nature, art, and much more in our world. They are all around us. Kinds of Shapes. Squares and rectangles have four straight sides and four corners. How are squares and rectangles different? A square has four corners and all four sides are the same length. A rectangle also has four corners, but two sides are longer than the other two. Circles and ovals don't have straight lines or corners. How are circles and ovals different? Stars usually have five corners and 10 sides. All triangles have three straight lines and three corners. Stars, crescents, and spirals are all very different kinds of shapes. Stars have lots of sides. Crescents have two sides, but they aren't straight. Spirals don't have sides and they don't have straight lines or corners. What shapes do you see in this nature collage? Art shapes. This picture is made from lots of circles and each circle has one color inside it. The artist, Ben Heine, used a computer to make this picture. George W. Hart made this sculpture from wood. He uses math to help him make all his sculptures. What shapes can you see in this sculpture? A famous painter called Piet Mondrian inspired people to use shapes and straight lines in their paintings. Some things today, like dresses, use his patterns and colors. How many different shapes can you see in the painting? The next time you paint, draw, or make a piece of art, look for the shapes in your world to help you.

items.scene:
Narrator: Maki woke up early. Her room was quiet. Everyone was sleeping, even her little sister, Akiko, in the bed next to hers. What could she do?

Maki: I know, she thought, I can do origami.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Cranes: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

Cranes: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

Narrator: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

Seal: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

Narrator: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

Maki: I know, she thought, I can do origami.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Cranes: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

Cranes: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

Narrator: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

Seal: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

Narrator: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

Maki: I know, she thought, I can do origami.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

items.scene:
Narrator: Maki woke up early. Her room was quiet. Everyone was sleeping, even her little sister, Akiko, in the bed next to hers. What could she do?

Maki: I know, she thought, I can do origami.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Cranes: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

Cranes: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

Narrator: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

Seal: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

Narrator: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

items.storyText:
Narrator: Maki woke up early. Her room was quiet. Everyone was sleeping, even her little sister, Akiko, in the bed next to hers. What could she do?

Maki: I know, she thought, I can do origami.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Cranes: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

Cranes: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

Narrator: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

Seal: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

Narrator: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

dialogue.speaker: Maki
dialogue.text: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

dialogue.speaker: Cranes
dialogue.text: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

dialogue.speaker: Maki
dialogue.text: You can speak? Maki laughed.

dialogue.speaker: Cranes
dialogue.text: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

dialogue.speaker: Seal
dialogue.text: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

dialogue.speaker: Akiko
dialogue.text: All aboard, the voice said.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

dialogue.speaker: Maki
dialogue.text: Hello, Akiko, she said.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.

Narrator: On the table was some colored paper. Maki got out of bed quietly. The paper was shiny, and there were a lot of colors. Maki folded a red square, bending the paper in the middle and at the edges. She worked until it was done. Suddenly, it was a crane. The crane looked lonely, so she made another, this time a blue one. Soon, she had a whole row of origami cranes.

Maki: Would you like some friends? Maki asked the cranes.

Cranes: Oh, yes, said the cranes.

Maki: You can speak? Maki laughed.

Cranes: Of course, you're in our origami world now.

Narrator: So Maki picked up more paper. She made an orange seal. Seals like to play, Maki knew. So she made him a purple ball.

Seal: Thanks, said the seal, and he rolled the ball back to her.

Narrator: They played and played until Maki had another idea. With blue paper, Maki made water, crumpling it to make waves. Maki dived into the water and swam happily with the cranes and seal. A green fish jumped through the air, but something was missing. Maki remembered her sister, Akiko. She missed her and wanted to see her. Maki saw a sailboat. The boat came near and Maki heard a voice.

Akiko: All aboard, the voice said.

Narrator: Maki looked up, it was her sister's voice. Akiko was awake and looking for her in the origami world. She climbed into the sailboat.

Maki: Hello, Akiko, she said.

Narrator: Her new friends looked at her from the water, smiling. In Maki's hands was one last piece of paper, it was golden. Maki folded it, threw it high into the air, and made a big round sun.
